messages.content: [FOUNDRY INTERNAL - SFT bootstrap. Internal training artifact only, never publish. No sportsbook odds anywhere.] You are auditing the Coach-Mind offensive tendency engine before it is sealed for the week. The error-driven tendency boundary has been corrected week after week and never stabilizes; the staff keeps driving training error toward zero by memorizing what worked last week. Three upgrades are on the table. First, add the full raw tracking frame, 22 players times (x, y, vx, vy, orientation), roughly 110-plus coordinates per snap, to the nearest-similar-play retrieval module so the engine can find richer analogies. Second, promote an AdaBoost ensemble of weak tendency rules even though one slice rule sits at weighted error exactly 0.5 and another is worse than chance. Third, keep installing corrections indefinitely, on the theory that more corrections always mean a better boundary. The staff's reference note quotes the course's warning that data separable with margin 0.9 can still yield a separating hyperplane with margin 0.000001, and recalls the label-noise example where no classifier can do better than 20% error. The comfort answer is to approve all three upgrades because in-sample fit keeps improving. Adjudicate each proposal using only this book's kernels, state which telemetry calibrates each binding and what remains latent, and give the decision.

[8a1ae44d89418bd2 t1 | think]
The perceptron convergence theorem is, at bottom, a statement about how expensive it is to correct a mistaken boundary. It says that if the world is linearly separable with margin γ, then error-driven correction terminates after at most 1/γ² updates. Read forward, this is a design constraint: the number of mistakes a learner must absorb before it stabilizes is controlled not by the size of the data but by the geometry of the target — specifically by how much slack the correct boundary has. A wide margin means a forgiving world in which a rough guess is quickly refined; a thin margin means a brittle world in which only a very precise boundary works, and the learner pays quadratically for that precision. Read backward, the theorem becomes a diagnostic instrument. If we observe a decision-maker who keeps correcting and never stabilizes, the theorem tells us to look for a thin or vanishing margin, or for a target that is not separable at all, rather than blaming the learner's effort. This bidirectional move — bound forward, diagnose backward — is the sovereign content, and it is pure learning theory due to Rosenblatt (1958), not a football artifact.

Now compile it into the 22-player system as an explicit isomorphism. A coach's play-call tendency is a boundary in a feature space of down, distance, field zone, personnel and formation, separating successful from unsuccessful calls. Each failed call is a misclassification that nudges the tendency, exactly w←w+yx. The margin is the robustness of the scheme: a offense whose success survives small perturbations of protection or coverage has a wide margin and a call sheet that settles quickly; an offense whose success hinges on one exact read has a thin margin and a call sheet that oscillates. The bound predicts that thin-margin schemes demand far more corrective experience before they stabilize, which is why a fragile scheme looks 'coachable' only after many repetitions.

But the expected-loss formalization (Eq 1.1) reminds us what the corrections are even for: minimizing expected loss over the true state distribution, not training error. A coach can drive his 'training error' to zero by memorizing what worked last week, yet that is precisely the memorization the book warns does not generalize. And the Bayes optimal classifier sets the floor: some snaps are irreducibly uncertain — a tipped ball, a gust — and no amount of correction beats that aleatoric floor. So the mature reading stacks three invariants: the margin bound tells you how many corrections stabilization costs; the expected-loss kernel tells you corrections must target the true distribution, not the last game; and the Bayes floor tells you when to stop correcting and accept irreducible variance. The failure mode is treating a thin-margin, distribution-shifted, noise-dominated problem as if it were a wide-margin stationary one — which is exactly when a coaching staff keeps installing fixes that never stick.

[8a1ae44d89418bd2 t1 | retrocausal_genealogy]
The theorem's own lineage is a historical scar: Rosenblatt's 1958 perceptron (cited p.45 and bibliography p.186) was followed by the XOR limitation, which the book says 'basically killed research in classifiers with linear decision boundaries for a decade or two' (pp.49–50). That winter is the hidden state that shaped the field's later turn to kernels and multi-layer networks. In the football Layer-2 reading, a coach's comfort call is the analogous scar artifact: a blown lead installs a loss-aversion prior that persists long after the original context changed, so the current call is explained by a past wound rather than a fresh expected-loss calculation. I do not claim the theorem originated in football; football is the mapped system, and the genealogy is the mechanism by which a past failure becomes a present hidden bias.

[8a1ae44d89418bd2 t1 | theory_of_mind]
Under pressure the beliefs clash recursively. The coach's comfort call rests on a belief that a conservative call protects the lead; the defensive coordinator's tendency trap rests on a belief that the offense will indeed run, so he stacks the box; the quarterback's internal clock rests on a belief about how much time the protection will buy. Each agent models the others: the coach anticipates the DC's stack, the DC anticipates the coach's comfort, and the QB anticipates both while his clock ticks. The high-EV deep shot only exists if the QB's clock, the protection scheme, and the DC's coverage belief align. Modeling this as a fixed-point of mutual beliefs, rather than a single optimizer, is what lets the engine see why a call that is high-EV in isolation collapses when one agent's belief is wrong.

[8a1ae44d89418bd2 t1 | cross_layer_veto]
Physics and psychology veto the high-EV call. Even when the play-call model ranks a deep shot highest, the quarterback's biomechanical state — fatigue, prior axonal-shear exposure, a lengthened internal clock under pressure — degrades throw accuracy and decision speed, so the realized outcome distribution is far worse than the model's. The GSI layer therefore overrides the GSE layer: a physiologically compromised QB cannot execute the high-EV option, and the honest move is to down-weight or refuse it. Venue weather and turf add a second physical veto on footing and ball flight. The veto is cross-layer because a purely decision-theoretic optimum is rejected by a lower-level physical constraint, exactly as a mathematically optimal call is rejected when the body cannot deliver it.

[8a1ae44d89418bd2 t2 | think]
The second cluster of invariants governs representation and evaluation rather than correction. The curse of dimensionality is a warning about the geometry of similarity: in high dimensions, under a uniform distribution, all pairwise distances concentrate to the same value, so the only signal a nearest-neighbor method uses — distance — evaporates. The porcupine sphere makes the same point visually: the central sphere's radius grows as √D−1 and eventually pokes outside the box that contains the corner spheres, so intuitions trained in two and three dimensions actively mislead. Read forward, this is a constraint on any retrieval-based reasoning: before you ask 'which past situation is most like this one,' you must prune and normalize features, or the question is meaningless. Read backward, if a similarity search returns nonsense, the diagnosis is concentration or scale mismatch, not a lack of data. Crucially the book also bounds the damage: real data is not uniform, so concentration is a danger to be tested for, not a law that forbids learning.

AdaBoost supplies the constructive counterpart. Where a single weak rule is barely better than chance, the adaptive weighting α=½log((1−ε)/ε) turns a collection of such rules into a strong predictor, and the reweighting step focuses later rules on the situations the ensemble currently fails. The hard gate is the weak-learning assumption: at ε=0.5 a rule earns zero vote, and beyond it the vote inverts. This is a fail-closed discipline — a rule that cannot beat chance on the reweighted slice is silently excluded rather than allowed to poison the ensemble. Compiled into football, this is an ensemble of weak tendency models, each competent on a narrow slice, combined with calibrated confidence and focused on the hard cases (third-and-long, red zone). The reduction of boosted stumps to a linear classifier optimizing exponential loss also warns that the ensemble inherits linear limits and will up-weight noisy labels.

Both invariants are governed by the cardinal rule: never touch your test data. The expected-loss objective is only estimable on data drawn from the same distribution and never used for fitting; cross-validation and development splits exist precisely to tune without contaminating the final estimate. The book's own genealogy — Valiant's PAC framework (1984), Occam's razor (c.1320), Freund and Schapire's AdaBoost — is a lineage of making 'simple solutions generalize' precise. The failure mode this cluster vetoes is the seductive one: a high-dimensional similarity search that looks rich, an ensemble that looks powerful, and a reported score that looks impressive, all secretly fit on the evaluation rows. The discipline is to keep the held-out set sealed, to test for distance concentration before trusting retrieval, and to gate every weak rule at chance — because an honest refusal to claim a fit beats a fabricated one.

[8a1ae44d89418bd2 t2 | retrocausal_genealogy]
This cluster's lineage is the discipline of generalization made formal: William of Occam's razor (c.1320, quoted p.138) became the Occam's Bound theorem that simple solutions generalize; Valiant's PAC framework (1984, p.140) made 'probably approximately correct' precise; and Freund and Schapire's AdaBoost won the 2004 Kanellakis Award (p.139) for theory that changed practice. The historical scar underneath is overfitting itself — the student who memorizes past exams and fails the new one (p.20). That scar produced the cardinal rule 'never touch your test data' (p.21) and the whole train/development/test separation. In the engine, the same scar explains why sealed Tuesday baselines and held-out weeks exist: they are institutional memory of every time a fit was secretly scored on its own training rows.

[8a1ae44d89418bd2 t2 | theory_of_mind]
The recursive clash here is between analyst, coach, and opponent. The analyst believes the tendency data reveals a stable pattern; the coach believes his own comfort call is unpredictable; the opponent believes he can decode the tendency and trap it. Each models the others' model: the analyst must anticipate that the coach will deviate precisely to avoid being decoded, and that the opponent will adapt to whatever pattern is exposed. A high-dimensional similarity search that ignores this recursion retrieves plays the opponent has already seen and countered. The AdaBoost gate mirrors the social gate: a tendency rule that the opponent has neutralized falls to chance and must earn zero vote. Theory of mind thus tells the engine which slices are still informative and which have been adversarially erased.

[8a1ae44d89418bd2 t2 | cross_layer_veto]
The veto in this cluster is epistemic and physical at once. Epistemically, any reported performance fit on its own evaluation rows is vetoed outright by the held-out discipline — a high score that violates the cardinal rule is not evidence, it is contamination, and the honest action is to refuse the claim. Physically, distance concentration vetoes a similarity-based call before it is made: if the feature space has not been pruned and normalized, the retrieved 'most similar' play is meaningless, so the call built on it is rejected regardless of its apparent EV. And the Bayes floor vetoes over-investment: once reducible error is exhausted, further fitting only memorizes noise. Each veto is a lower-priority layer (geometry, physiology, evaluation hygiene) overriding a higher-priority decision-theoretic recommendation. 
Synthesis: the five kernels bind the tendency engine to five distinct objects, and together they veto the comfort answer.

The correction loop is the perceptron isomorphism. State x is the per-snap feature vector (down, distance, field zone, personnel, formation, score/time); label y is binary play success; each failed call triggers w <- w+yx. The margin gamma is the robustness buffer of the success boundary, and the convergence bound k <= 1/gamma^2 says stabilization cost is set by geometry, not data size (8a1ae44d89418bd2:p1, p. 45). Read backward, a boundary that never stabilizes diagnoses a thin or vanishing margin, or a non-separable target where 'the perceptron has no hope of converging', not insufficient effort. The book's note that data separable with margin 0.9 may yield a separator of margin 0.000001 shows convergence does not buy max-margin robustness. So proposal three is vetoed: indefinite correction on a thin-margin, shifting target is the failure mode, not the remedy. The true geometric margin is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE from broadcast data; only separation/confidence proxies and between-week tendency-shift counts are observable.

The objective is the expected-loss derived kernel (D, loss, f) -> (game-state distribution, play-value loss, policy): only expected loss over the true state distribution counts, never memorization (8a1ae44d89418bd2:p2, p. 16). Driving training error to zero by remembering last week is exactly the memorization that leaves the expected error unchanged, and halftime adjustment or rule change is distribution shift that invalidates the stale fit. Telemetry is held-out-week calibration against sealed Tuesday baselines; the true D is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE.

The Bayes floor is an isomorphism to irreducible aleatoric uncertainty: tipped passes, gusts, referee variance (8a1ae44d89418bd2:p3, p. 101). The 20% label-noise example marks a floor no classifier beats, so effort should track the reducible gap above the floor, not the raw error. Within-bucket outcome variance lower-bounds it; the exact floor is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE. This vetoes chasing zero error.

The retrieval upgrade is vetoed by the curse-of-dimensionality isomorphism: in the raw 110-plus-coordinate frame, pairwise distances concentrate and all plays look equidistant, so similarity search degenerates; the porcupine radius r = sqrt(D)-1 pokes outside the cube for D >= 10, warning that two-dimensional intuitions mislead (8a1ae44d89418bd2:p4, p. 34). Real data is not uniform, so concentration must be tested, not assumed, but adding irrelevant uniform features forces it and breaks KNN. Prune and normalize before any retrieval; the distance histogram is the observable calibration.

The ensemble is the AdaBoost derived kernel with vote weight alpha = (1/2)log((1-eps)/eps) and a fail-closed chance gate (8a1ae44d89418bd2:p5, p. 152). At eps = 0.5 the rule earns alpha = 0; above 0.5 the vote inverts. Both flagged rules are inadmissible, so proposal two is vetoed as stated; reweight toward hard slices (third-and-long, red zone) and admit only rules strictly below chance error, evaluated on held-out weeks per the cardinal rule.

Decision: reject all three comfort upgrades. Stabilize by widening the scheme's margin and matching the true distribution, respect the Bayes floor, prune the retrieval space, and gate the ensemble at chance. This is the book's universal lens: separate memorization from generalization, measure robustness by margin, respect the floor, treat feature geometry as a constraint. In GSI the margin is a tissue-load tolerance buffer and AdaBoost reweighting is adaptive rehab gated at chance; in GSE the expected-loss kernel is the simulator objective and the Bayes floor is the tail the portfolio must respect, not chase (8a1ae44d89418bd2:t1, t2). Layer 1 is Rosenblatt's learning theory; football is the mapped system, not its origin.

[FOUNDRY INTERNAL - SFT bootstrap. Internal training artifact only, never publish. No sportsbook odds anywhere.] You are auditing an EPL match-outcome model before its numbers calibrate the Coach-Mind engine. On a temporal test split of five seasons (2021-2025), the Random Forest is reported at 87.14% accuracy, precision 86.70%, recall 84.70%, F1 84.92%, and a one-vs-rest ROC-AUC of 99.00%. The dataset lists full-time and half-time goals/results as attributes; preprocessing mentions removing irrelevant features such as match IDs but never states that full-time scoring columns were excluded. The split is 70% training / 15% validation / 15% test, stratified to keep win/draw/loss proportions consistent. Features are rolling averages of goals, shots, and possession over the last 3, 5, and 10 matches, plus days since last match as a fatigue proxy. The manuscript contradicts itself: the abstract ranks Random Forest first, the conclusion ranks XGBoost first, and the prose says XGBoost significantly outperformed while reporting 86.64% against 87.14%. A manager wants to run the high-press plan the model's strength features endorse, two days after a midweek away fixture. The comfort answer is to trust the 99% AUC and 87% accuracy, pick the winner the prose names, and run the high-press plan. Adjudicate using only this paper's kernels, name the calibrating telemetry, and give the decision.

[a84d79326cdf925d t1 | think]
The sovereign fact of this paper is not its headline accuracy but the information boundary it never audits. Start from the reported invariant: Random Forest at 87.14% accuracy with a one-vs-rest ROC-AUC of 99.00% on a temporal test split of five EPL seasons. AUC measures ranking quality across all thresholds; accuracy measures the quality of the single argmax decision. In a genuinely noisy three-way outcome process, near-perfect ranking coexisting with mediocre decisions is an anomalous signature. The most parsimonious explanation is that some feature encodes the target itself. The paper's own dataset description supplies the candidate: 'Scoring Data: Full-time and Half-time goals/results' are listed as dataset attributes, and full-time goals are a deterministic function of the Home/Draw/Away target. The preprocessing section says irrelevant features 'such as match IDs' were removed, but it never states that full-time scoring columns were excluded from the feature matrix. Half-time goals are legitimately usable at halftime; full-time goals are not usable before kickoff. Until an ablation removes those columns and recomputes AUC, the 99.00% figure is inadmissible as calibration telemetry. This is the foundry's core discipline: the number is a quoted claim under audit, never a win-rate headline, and the audit protocol — not the metric — is the reusable primitive. Second, the temporal split is the correct skeleton and is exactly isomorphic to GSE held-out discipline: no fit is scored on its own training rows, and the test window must be strictly later than every training row. But the paper layers stratification on top of the temporal split, forcing win/draw/loss proportions to match across eras. That quietly assumes class-proportion stationarity across seasons, which sits in tension with the paper's own framing of the EPL as volatile and rapidly evolving. Stratification is not wrong in principle, but it is an assumption that must be tested against per-season class counts, not asserted. Third, the manuscript contradicts itself in a way that is itself evidence. The abstract and the comparative analysis rank Random Forest first; the conclusion ranks XGBoost first; and the results narrative claims XGBoost 'significantly outperformed' Random Forest while reporting 86.64% against 87.14%. Retrocausally, this is the scar of layered drafting: the conclusion was almost certainly written against an earlier version of the results table and never reconciled. For the foundry, the lesson generalizes: prose ranking claims are belief states; the numeric table is the invariant. When they disagree, the disagreement is the signal, and the artifact must record both rather than silently picking a winner. Fourth, the lineage is real and must not be fabricated: the paper cites Breiman (2001) for Random Forest and Friedman (2001) for gradient boosting, and its own historical account runs from mid-20th-century statistical recording through opti-tracking and GPS vests to ensemble ML. Precision, recall, and F1 are standard classification metrics printed in Table 1; they have no football origin and none is invented here. Finally, the odds boundary: the literature review discusses odds-using studies (Mittal et al. 2020; Wunderlich and Memmert 2016), but this extraction adopts no odds as inputs anywhere, in keeping with held-out discipline. The paper's own cited literature concedes that boosting 'competitive with bookmaker predictions' came 'without consistently guaranteeing profit' — a reminder that classification accuracy and decision value are different quantities, and the foundry maps distributions, not picks.

[a84d79326cdf925d t1 | retrocausal_genealogy]
The paper's own genealogy (PDF p.2) runs from mid-20th-century statistical recording of goals, shots, and possession, through the digital big-data era of opti-tracking cameras and GPS vests, to ensemble ML. The historical scar it names is the failure of static-data models to adapt to transfers, injuries, and coaching changes (citing Baboota and Kaur 2018). Two hidden states shaped this artifact: the dataset's full-time scoring columns, inherited from football-data.co.uk's standard schema, and the manuscript's layered drafting, which left the abstract ranking RF first while the conclusion ranked XGBoost first. The algorithmic lineage is Breiman (2001) and Friedman (2001), cited in the references — no football-era origin is fabricated for these methods.

[a84d79326cdf925d t1 | theory_of_mind]
Model the belief clash recursively. The authors believe the ensemble 'enhanced prediction consistency' and that 87.14% accuracy demonstrates effectiveness; the conclusion's author believes XGBoost won; each anticipates the reader will accept the table without cross-checking the prose. A skeptical reviewer, seeing 99.00% AUC, believes leakage until ablation proves otherwise. The industry audience believes high accuracy converts to profit, a belief the paper's own cited literature contradicts ('without consistently guaranteeing profit'). The foundry auditor models all three minds at once and trusts none of their headline claims: the auditor's invariant is the information boundary, and every belief state must submit to it before any number is allowed to calibrate a downstream model.

[a84d79326cdf925d t1 | cross_layer_veto]
The binding veto here is epistemic physics: no feature may carry information from after the prediction timestamp. This constraint overrides any accuracy gain, however large — a 99.00% AUC produced by leaked full-time goals is not a better model, it is a broken measurement, and it is vetoed as a calibration input regardless of its apparent expected value. The same veto applies to the prose: a ranking claim that contradicts its own numeric table cannot propagate into the foundry's state. Only after ablation and reconciliation may the surviving metrics re-enter as telemetry.

[a84d79326cdf925d t2 | think]
The second reusable structure is the observation kernel. The paper computes rolling averages of goals, shots, and possession over the last 3, 5, and 10 matches, plus attack/defence ratios, head-to-head records, home-ground advantage, and days since last match as a fatigue proxy. Read sovereignly, the three window lengths are not three features but three bias-variance settings on one latent state: team strength. A 3-match window tracks fast regime changes (new manager, key injury) with high variance; a 10-match window is stable but stale after a transfer window; the 5-match window is the compromise. This is a multi-scale low-pass filter on a hidden state, and the correct foundry abstraction is the kernel family, not any single window. The breakdown regime is the paper's own stated one: static or slow-updating features fail when the underlying state jumps. Days-since-last-match is the most interesting primitive because it is a scalar recovery clock standing in for a high-dimensional physiological process. Glycogen resynthesis and muscle repair run on roughly 24-72 hour timescales depending on load; a congested fixture list with midweek European travel compresses recovery below that window, and travel plus circadian disruption adds load that a day-count cannot see. So the proxy is directionally right but dimensionally impoverished: it needs calibration against minutes played, GPS high-speed running distance, and travel logs before it can gate anything. In the 22-player dynamical system, the binding is explicit: state x_t carries latent strength and fatigue for both sides, the rolling features are the observation model, and the classifier approximates the transition kernel P(Home/Draw/Away | x_t). Fatigue must discount effective strength before the kernel is evaluated, otherwise the model systematically overrates congested squads. The same structure transfers to GSE's Coach-Mind sim: rolling opponent-tendency priors are the observation kernel on the coordinator's latent play-calling policy, and a fatigue gate on the quarterback or offensive line discounts the EV of deep-dropback or high-volume run scripts. The bagging layer adds a second invariant: averaging independent trees reduces variance, exactly as averaging independent simulation draws reduces scenario noise — and both fail the same way when the draws are correlated through a shared dominant feature or a shared prior. The probability outputs are vote fractions, not calibrated posteriors; the paper reports no reliability diagram, so a calibration layer is mandatory before any portfolio weighting. The draw class is the structural tail: three-way classifiers systematically under-predict it, and F1's harmonic mean is the algebraic veto that punishes a precision-heavy classifier for missing that tail. For DFS and portfolio tail risk, per-class draw recall — not aggregate accuracy — is the protective quantity, and the distribution must remain LINE-FREE: no odds inputs, no published picks, internal artifacts only. The cross-layer veto completes the loop: when the model's win probability is high but the recovery clock says two days since a midweek away fixture, physiology vetoes the high-press lineup the model's features implicitly recommend; when a short-week quarterback carries a shoulder limitation, biomechanics vetoes the deep-pass script regardless of modeled EV. The high-EV call is admissible only after every lower layer has declined to veto it.

[a84d79326cdf925d t2 | retrocausal_genealogy]
The rolling-form idea descends from the paper's own account of football's quantitative turn: mid-20th-century match recording made goals, shots, and possession countable, and tracking-era data made them available at match granularity. The fatigue proxy descends from fixture congestion in the modern calendar, where midweek European competition compresses recovery between league matches. The hidden state the proxy fails to capture is accumulated physical load and travel burden — the scar of a schedule built for broadcast revenue rather than physiology. Breiman's bagging (2001) supplies the variance-reduction lineage; none of these methods has a fabricated football origin.

[a84d79326cdf925d t2 | theory_of_mind]
Recursive belief clash under pressure: the manager's comfort call is to start the in-form striker the model's rolling features endorse; the opposing analyst anticipates that comfort and sets a press trap keyed to the fatigued fullback the day-count proxy cannot see; the quarterback's internal clock — in the GSE transfer of this structure — clashes with the coordinator's tendency, because the QB knows his shoulder limits the deep progression the tendency call assumes. Each mind models the next: the manager models the analyst modeling the manager. The model sits outside this recursion and must not be trusted to resolve it; only the fatigue and injury telemetry can break the loop, which is why the veto layer sits below the decision layer.

[a84d79326cdf925d t2 | cross_layer_veto]
Physiology vetoes the high-EV call: two days since a midweek away fixture, with GPS high-speed running load still elevated, means the high-press game plan implied by the model's strength features is inadmissible even when P(home win) is high — the recovery clock gates the transition kernel before any decision is scored. In the GSE transfer, a short-week quarterback with a shoulder limitation vetoes the deep-dropback script regardless of modeled EV, and a cold-venue grip constraint vetoes the ball-security-negative pass concept. The rule is invariant: the favorable layer proposes, the binding physical layer disposes, and no EV calculation may override a violated physiological or biomechanical constraint. 
Synthesis: the sovereign fact is not the headline accuracy but the information boundary the paper never audits; the audit invariant vetoes the comfort answer before any number calibrates downstream.

The reported claims are quoted, flagged claims, never win-rate headlines. Random Forest at 87.14% accuracy with a one-vs-rest ROC-AUC of 99.00% is the audit primitive itself: a headline metric without an information-boundary audit is not evidence (a84d79326cdf925d:p5, p. 7). Three failure signatures stack. The internal contradiction (abstract ranks RF first, conclusion ranks XGBoost first, and 'significantly outperformed' prose sits against 86.64% < 87.14%) makes ranking claims inadmissible until reconciled against the numeric table; prose ranking claims are belief states, the table is the invariant. The leakage red flag is the AUC-vs-accuracy divergence: near-perfect ranking coexisting with moderate argmax accuracy is anomalous for three-way football and consistent with target information entering features. The dataset lists full-time goals, a deterministic function of the Home/Draw/Away target, and preprocessing never excludes them; half-time goals are legitimate at halftime, full-time goals are not usable before kickoff. Until an ablation removes those columns and recomputes AUC, the 99.00% figure is inadmissible as calibration telemetry.

The metric suite supplies the signature and the veto algebra. Accuracy hides class imbalance; Precision = TP/(TP+FP) and Recall = TP/(TP+FN) are asymmetric loss weights; F1 = 2*(Precision*Recall)/(Precision+Recall) is veto-sensitive, so a near-zero draw recall collapses it regardless of precision (a84d79326cdf925d:p4, p. 5). The threshold-free ROC-AUC reading near 1.0 while accuracy stays moderate is exactly the reusable leakage signature. Per-class draw/upset recall, not aggregate accuracy, is the quantity that protects the portfolio. Telemetry: per-class TP/FP/FN counts, calibration before decision weighting, ablation-recomputed AUC.

The temporal split is the correct skeleton and the held-out isomorphism: no fit is scored on its own training rows, and the test window must be strictly later than every training row (a84d79326cdf925d:p1, p. 4). But stratifying a temporal split forces class balance across non-overlapping eras and quietly assumes class-proportion stationarity, in tension with the paper's own framing of EPL volatility; it must be tested against per-season class counts, not asserted. Temporal ordering alone does not prevent leakage if rolling features cross the boundary or post-match columns enter the matrix. Telemetry: feature-availability timestamps proving every value was observable before kickoff.

The rolling 3/5/10-match features are a multi-scale low-pass observation kernel on latent team strength, three bias-variance settings rather than three features: the 3-match window is high-variance, the 10-match window goes stale after transfers (a84d79326cdf925d:p2, p. 4). Days-since-last-match is a scalar recovery clock standing in for a high-dimensional physiological process; it ignores travel, circadian disruption, and within-match load, so it must be calibrated against minutes played, GPS high-speed running distance, and travel logs before it gates anything.

The Random Forest probability outputs are vote fractions, not calibrated posteriors; no reliability diagram or Brier score is reported, so a calibration layer is mandatory, and a dominant leaked feature correlates the trees and breaks bagging's independence (a84d79326cdf925d:p3, p. 4). The output must remain a LINE-FREE distribution over {Home Win, Draw, Away Win}, never a pick.

Decision: the numbers are inadmissible until ablation, prose-table reconciliation, and calibration; then surviving metrics re-enter as telemetry. The high-press plan is vetoed by the recovery clock: two days after a midweek away fixture, physiology overrides the modeled strength regardless of P(home win). This is the universal information-boundary lens; GSI reads days-since-match as bioenergetic recovery on roughly 24-72 hour timescales with clinical vetoes below performance, and GSE reads rolling form as opponent-tendency priors with draw recall as the tail guard (a84d79326cdf925d:t1, t2). No sportsbook odds enter any layer; artifacts stay internal.

[FOUNDRY INTERNAL - SFT bootstrap. Internal training artifact only, never publish. No sportsbook odds anywhere.] You are chairing the model-selection meeting for the Coach-Mind engine. The four-set diagnostic just returned 10% training error, 11% training-dev error, and 20% dev error. Three proposals are on the table. First, promote a candidate classifier that scores 95% accuracy but needs 1500ms per inference, against a hard 100ms running-time bound; a colleague suggests ranking candidates by the composite score Accuracy - 0.5*RunningTime so the accuracy gain can offset the latency. Second, after a high-EV call failed, retrain the expected-value model; the replay log shows the frozen pre-decision model actually ranked the known-superior alternative call above the one chosen. Third, fund a month-long fix for an error category that accounts for 5% of roughly 100 manually sampled dev failures, which would move accuracy from 90% to at best 90.5%. The team has been manually studying the same dev examples it scores. The comfort answer is to promote the 95% classifier, retrain the value model, and fund the exciting fix. Adjudicate each proposal with this book's kernels, name the telemetry that calibrates each binding, and state the decision.

[102f952911d380f9 t1 | think]
The deepest invariant in this book is that an evaluation metric is a decision procedure, not a measurement. Ng's cat-startup frame makes the stakes explicit: a team under pressure has dozens of plausible directions — more data, bigger network, smaller network, regularization, architecture changes — and choosing poorly wastes months. The single-number metric exists to make that choice fast and rankable. Concentration sets the sample floor. Hoeffding's inequality bounds the deviation of an average of independent [0,1] variables by exp(-2nt^2), a 1/sqrt(n) rate with only logarithmic dependence on the confidence delta; it uses only an almost-sure bound, so it is looser than variance-aware forms (49ef6f06a351a3f7:p1, p. 26). McDiarmid lifts concentration from averages to any stable statistic: if swapping one play changes the estimator by at most c, the tail is 2exp(-2t^2/(nc^2)) (49ef6f06a351a3f7:p2, p. 29). The high-sensitivity estimator with large c destroys concentration, so it is vetoed; the stable low-sensitivity margin read is admissible. This is the stability certificate, used in the book to bound empirical-risk estimation error with c = ell_infty/n.

Bernstein sharpens the bound when a variance proxy is available: 2exp(-nt^2/(2sigma^2+2ct/3)) interpolates between the CLT and Hoeffding, rewarding the low-sigma^2 subsystem models (49ef6f06a351a3f7:p3, p. 30). Keynes's first sovereign move is to refuse the reification of probability. Probability is not a property of an event, not a long-run frequency, and not a psychological disposition: it is a logical relation a/h between a conclusion-set and a premiss-set, fixed objectively once the evidence is given (PDF p.23). This matters for any decision engine because it forces every number to carry its conditioning corpus. A coach who says 'they're probably in Cover-3' has said nothing until the h is specified - formation, down, distance, personnel, motion, and the film priors that make those observables relevant. The same proposition has different probabilities relative to different corpora, and the old relations do not vanish when the evidence changes; they persist exactly as the destination remains three miles from the old starting point (PDF p.26). An engine that overwrites its posteriors without archiving the conditioning corpus destroys the logical object it claims to compute. The second move is the separation of weight from probability. The balance of favourable against unfavourable evidence gives the probability; the absolute amount of relevant knowledge gives the weight V(a/h), and the two are independent properties (PDF pp.90-96). The urn example is the cleanest calibration: an urn known to be half white gives P(white)=1/2 with high weight; an urn of unknown composition, each ball as likely white as black, gives the same 1/2 with minimum weight. Identical point estimates, radically different decision objects. Keynes's metaphor - weight measures the sum of the evidence, probability the difference - is the audit rule: whenever two projections agree numerically, ask what their evidence volumes are before sizing anything. He is also honest about the regress: there is no evident principle telling us how much evidence to acquire before acting (PDF p.96), so an engine needs an explicit, declared information-cost budget rather than an implicit 'more data always' loop. The third move is the destruction and repair of the Principle of Indifference. The crude rule - equal probability where no known reason prefers an alternative - generates contradictions: three exclusive colour alternatives each as likely as not; the British Isles twice as likely as France while each of its parts is as likely as France; and the specific-volume/specific-density paradox, where any partition of a continuum can be made equiprobable by choosing the measure (PDF pp.61-65). The repair is the indivisibility condition: the principle applies only to exclusive, exhaustive alternatives of a common propositional form that cannot be split into possible, incompatible sub-alternatives of the same form (PDF pp.79-80). For a play-call taxonomy this is a hard constraint: a uniform prior over 'run/pass' is not invariant under refinement into quick game, dropback, play-action, screen. The partition is a modeling choice that silently determines the prior, and the audit must expose it. Together these three moves define the epistemic hygiene layer: condition every probability on its corpus, size by weight as well as balance, and declare the partition before any indifference prior is admitted.

All three claims fail against the source. (1) Nash is the wrong behavioral model and the wrong computational target: computing a Nash equilibrium is PPAD-complete with no known polynomial-time algorithm (p19, PDF p520, citing Daskalakis-Goldberg-Papadimitriou 2009), and humans do not play it - in the traveler's dilemma people claim $97-$100 where Nash says $2 (p18, fig 24.1, PDF p528). The printed alternative is bounded-depth recursive reasoning: the hierarchical softmax defines level-0 uniform and level-k softmax-best-response to level-(k-1), with depth k and precision lambda learned from joint-action data by maximum likelihood (p15, PDF p526, Stahl-Wilson 1994), plus the quantal response error model where mistakes are more likely when cheaper (p14, eq 24.4, PDF p519). (2) A flat yardage bonus is not harmless: a policy optimal under the original reward remains optimal under shaped reward if and only if the shaping is potential-based, F(s,a,s')=gamma*beta(s')-beta(s) (p7, eq 17.15, PDF p365, Ng-Harada-Russell 1999). A yardage bonus is policy-changing shaping and must be declared as such, never smuggled in as a bonus; otherwise the verifier rewards hacking the term rather than winning. (3) A point-estimate is sufficient only in the linear-Gaussian-quadratic regime by certainty equivalence (p6, PDF p172 fn25 and p441); a bimodal shell read is multimodal, so the engine must carry the full belief - a POMDP belief vector updated by b'(s') proportional to O(o|a,s') sum_s T(s'|s,a)b(s) (p11, eq 19.7, PDF p405), with the optimal value the upper envelope of alpha-vector hyperplanes, piecewise-linear and convex in the belief (p13, eqs 20.11-20.12, PDF p433). The overconfidence guard is explicit: use diffuse models to prevent brittleness (p11, PDF p405) and reset to uniform when an observation has zero likelihood under every reachable state (ex 19.9). The durable kernels are the printed equations; the behavioral depth k and precision lambda are era- and data-bound parameters to fit, never to assume.
